hero.title: Mercedes-AMG M177 Engine - Replacement Cost, Problems & Compatibility
hero.description: The M177 is Mercedes-AMG’s revolutionary 4.0-litre "Hot-Vee" V8 biturbo petrol engine, famous for placing the twin turbochargers inside the cylinder V for instant throttle response. Fitted to the W205 C63, W213 E63, W463 G63, and W222 S63, reconditioned M177 engines typically start from £7,000 , serving as the definitive modern powerhouse for high-performance AMG builds and restorations.

costGuide.title: Mercedes-AMG M177 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an M177 engine typically takes 16-24 hours at £85-£110/hr (AMG specialist) - the "Hot-Vee" layout and tight engine bays (especially in the C63 and G63) make extraction highly labour-intensive.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the condition of the cylinder bores, the twin turbochargers, and the hot-vee oil feed lines. Because early M177 engines are prone to cylinder scoring, reputable recon specialists will typically borescope the block, install Darton iron cylinder sleeves if scoring is present, and upgrade the turbo oil feed lines to prevent immediate post-installation failures. For a full breakdown of market rates, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Mercedes-AMG M177 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Cylinder Wall Scoring (Alusil Block Wear)
items.whatHappens: The M177 features an Alusil (aluminum-silicon) coated cylinder block. Under high boost, immense thermal loads, and specific lateral G-forces, the piston skirts can wear through the factory coating, causing vertical scoring in the cylinder walls (most commonly cylinders 4 and 8). This manifests as a distinct metallic ticking or knocking noise, excessive oil consumption, and misfires.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, the block can be machined and fitted with aftermarket Darton iron cylinder sleeves to permanently resolve the issue. If the scoring has damaged the pistons or connecting rods, a full rebuilt M177 short block or complete engine is required.

items.title: Hot-Vee Turbo Oil Line Coking and Leaks
items.whatHappens: By placing the twin turbochargers inside the "V" of the engine, AMG achieved incredible throttle response but created an extreme heat environment. The rubber and plastic turbo oil feed and return lines bake over time, leading to external oil leaks onto the hot exhaust (creating smoke and a fire risk) or internal coking that starves the turbo bearings of lubrication.
items.repairVsReplace: Upgrading to high-temperature silicone or braided stainless steel oil lines is a mandatory preventative measure. If the turbos have already suffered bearing failure due to oil starvation, they must be rebuilt or replaced.

items.title: Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
items.whatHappens: As a direct injection engine, fuel does not wash over the back of the intake valves. Combined with the PCV system routing oil vapours into the intake tract, hard carbon deposits bake onto the valves, restricting airflow.
items.repairVsReplace: This causes rough idling, hesitation, and reduced power. The definitive repair is a professional "walnut blasting" service to clean the intake ports and valves.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2019 models feature revised piston skirt coatings, improved cylinder honing processes from the factory, and updated turbo oil line materials, significantly reducing the risk of cylinder scoring and making them the most robust examples of the M177 family .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes-AMG M177.980
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, near the bellhousing, accompanied by the iconic handwritten signature plaque of the AMG engine builder ("One Man, One Engine"). It will also be listed on your V5C logbook or visible via a VIN decode. The M177.980 is the primary wet-sump variant used across the C, E, S, and G-Class AMG ranges. It is sometimes confused with the M178 (the dry-sump variant used exclusively in the AMG GT sports car) or the M176 (the non-AMG, lower-output 4.0L V8 used in the S 580 / GLS 580). Fitting the wrong revision matters significantly: the M177 features specific AMG engine mounts, high-flow turbo plumbing, and aggressive ECU mapping that will not function correctly if swapped with an M176, and physically will not bolt up to the AMG GT's transaxle subframe without the M178 dry sump.

the legendary 6.2L naturally aspirated V8 that preceded the forced-induction era, sharing the "One Man, One Engine" hand-built philosophy but lacking the colossal low-end torque of the M177.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement M177 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: Buying a used M177 engine carries extreme financial risk unless a professional borescope inspection of all eight cylinders has been performed to rule out Alusil cylinder scoring. Given the £5,000+ cost of machining and sleeving a scored block, purchasing a used unit with unknown history or without verified bore health is highly discouraged.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned M177 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the fatal flaws by borescoping and sleeving the cylinders if necessary, upgrading the hot-vee turbo oil lines to high-temperature materials, performing a walnut blast carbon clean, and renewing all turbo seals.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full M177 engine rebuild is highly justified for W213 E 63 S or W463 G 63 AMG builds where maximum horsepower, track use, or off-road reliability is required. An upgraded rebuild should include forged pistons, upgraded connecting rods, and precision-balanced rotating assemblies to handle well over 700 hp.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your M177 engine is installed by specialists equipped to handle the complex Hot-Vee plumbing and AMG electronics, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the M177 is found in modern AMG vehicles valued between £30,000 and £120,000+, a full engine replacement is a financially viable necessity to protect the asset's value. However, due to the high cost of the engine and the specialized labour required, always ensure the replacement cost does not exceed the vehicle's current market valuation .

items.question: How much does a Mercedes M177 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes-AMG M177 engine typically costs between £7,000 and £11,000 for supply only . Fitted costs generally range from £9,000 to £14,000 depending on the specialist, while used units can be found from £4,000 but carry an extreme financial risk due to the potential for Alusil cylinder wall scoring. → Compare M177 engine replacement quotes today

items.question: What is the most common failure on the M177 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are cylinder wall scoring (Alusil block wear), hot-vee turbo oil line coking, and intake valve carbon buildup. Cylinder scoring causes metallic ticking and excessive oil consumption, while coked oil lines can starve the twin turbos of lubrication, leading to catastrophic bearing failure. → Get quotes for a rebuilt M177 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the M177.980 engine?
items.answer: The M177.980 was fitted to the W205 C-Class (C 63 AMG), the W213 E-Class (E 63 AMG), the W222 S-Class (S 63 AMG), the W463 G-Class (G 63 AMG), and the X253 GLC-Class (GLC 63 AMG), serving as the definitive Hot-Vee V8 for these high-performance chassis from 2015 onwards. → Check your registration to confirm your exact M177 fitment

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned M177 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned M177 is strongly recommended over a used unit. A proper rebuild will proactively address the fatal Alusil scoring flaw by installing Darton iron cylinder sleeves, upgrading the hot-vee oil lines to high-temperature materials, and performing a walnut blast carbon clean, whereas a used engine with unknown history risks immediate, catastrophic bore failure. → Compare reconditioned M177 engine prices from UK specialists

items.answer: The M177.980 is the wet-sump variant for C, E, S, G, and GLC AMG models. The M178 is the dry-sump variant exclusively for the AMG GT, and the M176 is the non-AMG 4.0L V8.
